title: Fine log schemes, their morphisms and relative etale tests
statement: A fine log scheme is a locally Noetherian scheme $X$ [pqf-def-locnoeth] with an etale log structure $M$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] satisfying the fine-chart predicate of [def-trf-fine-log-etale-descent-datum]; saturation is not required. A morphism $(Y,N)\to(X,M)$ is a scheme map $f:Y\to X$ together with the structure-preserving map $f^{-1}M\to N$ of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Its relative-test presentation assigns, to $W\to X$, $V\to Y$ in the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and $k:V\to W$ with $kW=Vf$, a natural monoid homomorphism $M(W)\to N(V)$ compatible with pullback of regular functions. Equality with a composite includes the equation of scheme maps and equality of the composed section maps on every composable relative test diagram. Equality of two composites through different intermediate fine log schemes is tested on every pair of such diagrams with the same composite test map. If the underlying scheme map is etale, strictness means these section maps are bijective whenever $k$ is an isomorphism of schemes: this identifies $N$ with the restriction of $M$ under the localized-site equivalence. For any etale map $p:T\to X$, write $M(p)$ for its sections on this object; for $h:T'\to T$ with $ph$ etale, restriction $M(p)\to M(ph)$ is the original sheaf restriction.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1, printed p.69 (fine versus fs, locally Noetherian convention, log morphisms); VIII 3.3.4(ii) and 3.3.8, printed pp.107--108 (strict etale charts and descent).
